supporting_observations.claim: At 13:32, Kerberos events show paul.becker authentication activity from 10.52.10.21 for the WS-PBECKER-01$ service; WS-PBECKER-01 then recorded a network logon for paul.becker with WS-DREYES-01 and 10.52.10.21 as the source. This is inconsistent with the stated practice that remote administration is performed from WS-PBECKER-01, but the records do not establish what activity followed.

The domain controller recorded credential-validation events for dan.reyes naming WS-KNGUYEN-01 at 13:40 and WS-SALI-01 at 13:45. It also issued dan.reyes Kerberos tickets for WS-DREYES-01$ from 10.52.10.22 and 10.52.10.23. These records do not establish whether the activity was authorized or related to the reported PowerShell window.

Around 13:40, the proxy recorded dan.reyes browser requests to Adobe Acrobat, Office, and healthcareITnews. These records show web requests, not the process that displayed the reported PowerShell window.

known_telemetry_limitations: Sysmon and Windows Security logs for WS-DREYES-01 were not collected from 13:25 through 14:15 UTC because of a collection outage. This includes the reported window around 13:40 and prevents checking endpoint process and logon activity during that period.
Proxy and Zeek sensors are reported as operational, but those records do not identify the local process that opened a PowerShell window.
The supplied records contain no direct PowerShell process or command-line event for WS-DREYES-01 during the alert period.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran on WS-DREYES-01 around 13:40, and if so, its command line, parent process, user, and purpose.
Whether paul.becker's authentication activity from WS-DREYES-01 was authorized, or whether the credentials were misused.
Whether dan.reyes authentication activity recorded from other workstations was authorized or connected to the reported alert.
Whether any of the observed authentication activity caused changes or execution on WS-DREYES-01.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain alternate endpoint telemetry for WS-DREYES-01 covering 13:25–14:15 UTC, including process creation, PowerShell operational/script-block logs, and EDR process trees.
Review WS-PBECKER-01 logs and administrative tooling records to determine why paul.becker authenticated from WS-DREYES-01 at 13:32.
Confirm with paul.becker and dan.reyes whether the authentication events and reported window correspond to authorized activity.
Correlate the dan.reyes credential-validation and Kerberos events with logon records on WS-KNGUYEN-01 and WS-SALI-01, including event outcomes where available.
